name: Thailand
headline: Thailand: +2.4% growth in 2025, −0.1% inflation, debt 65% of GDP
sections: Thailand is a $577 billion economy (2025), the world's 31st-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +2.4% in 2025, slower than the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $26K at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 23.7% of GDP (2025).
Consumer prices rose −0.1% in 2025, in deflation, down from 6.1% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 1.0% (2025), below the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 4.5% (2025).
Gross government debt is 65% of GDP (2025), a elevated level that has risen from 49% in 2020. The general government balance is −1.7% of GDP (2025).
The current account balance is +3.0% of GDP (2025). Trade equals 138% of GDP (2025), a highly open economy. Net FDI inflows were 3.2% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 70% of GDP by 2031, still rising from today's level. Life expectancy is 76.6 years (2024). Population: 71.6 million (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
